files.description: Clinic appointments in New York (160 rows, February to November 2025, so the clock changes in March and November fall inside the data): appt_id (whole number), local_start (New York wall-clock start, text YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, no UTC offset), start_with_offset (the same moment as ISO text with its UTC offset, e.g. "2025-06-13T08:45:00-04:00"), clinic (Harbor, Midtown or Riverside; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty).

task_text: Each appointment needs a reminder exactly one calendar day before it, at the same New York wall-clock time (local_start is New York local time). `result` should be a table with the columns appt_id and reminder, where reminder is ISO 8601 text including the UTC offset that applies in New York at the reminder time (for example '2025-06-12T08:45:00-04:00'), in file order.
intended_computation: For each of the 160 appointments take the New York wall-clock start minus one calendar day and write it as ISO text with the offset valid in New York at that moment (-05:00 in winter, -04:00 in summer).

predicted_direction.reason: with the 2.x time-zone library the stdlib date arithmetic keeps the old UTC offset across the clock change; 3.x gives the correct offset

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 in package TASKS_M1; task text, card, naive solution, reference and predicted direction were prepared there.
